subsystems.name: Microwave resonator
subsystems.role: holds the qubit's microwave excitation in a superconducting circuit.
parts: high-Q superconducting thin-film inductor and capacitor

subsystems.name: Coupling element
subsystems.role: the active medium that shifts optical behaviour in response to a microwave field.
parts: thin-film lithium niobate waveguide or ring (electro-optic)
or a suspended nanobeam/membrane with a shared optical and mechanical mode

subsystems.name: Optical cavity
subsystems.role: enhances the interaction and defines the telecom wavelength mode.

subsystems.name: Cryogenic package
subsystems.role: keeps thermal photons far below one per mode and brings signals in and out.
parts: superconducting wiring to the qubit chip
optical fibre feedthroughs with low heat leak

subsystems.name: Pump and control
subsystems.role: supplies the laser pump and microwave tones that drive the conversion.

subsystems.name: Verification chain
subsystems.role: proves the transfer is quantum, not classical.

buildSteps.title: Design matched modes
buildSteps.detail: Choose the microwave and optical cavity linewidths so the two decay rates are equal — the condition for impedance matching and the highest conversion efficiency.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the microwave circuit
buildSteps.detail: Superconducting niobium or aluminium films are deposited on a low-loss substrate and patterned into resonators with lithography.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the photonic chip
buildSteps.detail: Thin-film lithium niobate or silicon-on-insulator is patterned by electron-beam lithography and etched into waveguides and ring resonators.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the two
buildSteps.detail: The photonic chip and superconducting circuit are aligned with sub-micron precision and bonded, so one optical mode and one microwave mode overlap in the same volume.

buildSteps.title: Package and fibre-couple
buildSteps.detail: Optical fibres are attached to the chip and superconducting wiring run to the qubit, all inside a shielded enclosure.

buildSteps.title: Cool to millikelvin
buildSteps.detail: The assembly goes into a dilution refrigerator so that thermal photons cannot swamp the single-photon signal.

buildSteps.title: Characterise
buildSteps.detail: Laser light is sent in and microwave photons out (and vice versa); efficiency, bandwidth and added noise are measured.

buildSteps.title: Close the link
buildSteps.detail: Two qubits are connected through optical fibre and entanglement between them is verified.

prerequisites.why: they hold the microwave photon long enough to interact with the optical mode.

prerequisites.tech: Low-loss integrated photonics (thin-film lithium niobate, silicon)
prerequisites.why: needed for strong electro-optic coupling and long optical storage times on a chip.
thermal noise must be well under one photon at microwave frequencies.
without them a quantum conversion cannot be distinguished from a classical one.

prerequisites.tech: Efficient, low-noise coupling at the single-photon level
prerequisites.why: no device yet combines high efficiency with added noise below one photon at useful bandwidth.

pathway.milestone: table-top demonstrations converting microwave and optical photons, mostly at efficiencies from a fraction of a per cent up to tens of per cent with narrow bandwidth
pathway.unlocks: proof that the two frequency domains can be linked.

pathway.milestone: devices with high efficiency, near-quantum-limited added noise and megahertz-scale bandwidth
pathway.unlocks: faithful transfer of qubit states over metres of fibre.

pathway.milestone: entanglement distributed between two superconducting qubits via optical fibre
pathway.unlocks: modular quantum processors and the first quantum repeater nodes.

pathway.milestone: transducers integrated into repeater chains and networked quantum computers
pathway.unlocks: a quantum internet in which microwave qubits talk over today's telecom fibre.
